scenes.question: Do two rulers move together, or do they actually agree?

beats.say: Imagine two kitchen scales. Whenever you add flour, both numbers go up together. But one always reads half a kilo heavier. They are perfectly correlated, and still they do not agree.

That is why correlation is not enough. Formula twenty-three, Bland-Altman agreement, measures agreement directly: the average difference between harmonised MODIS and observed VIIRS, called the bias, and the range within which ninety-five percent of differences fall.

parts.say: For each month t, we start with a, the harmonised MODIS value, and take its log, after adding a half so that empty months still work.
Then we subtract the log of b, what VIIRS really observed. On the log scale, a difference means a ratio: zero means a perfect match. The sign is fixed: harmonised minus observed.
d bar is the average of all those differences. That is the bias. If it is close to zero, harmonised MODIS is neither too high nor too low on average.
And plus or minus 1.96 standard deviations gives the limits of agreement: the band where about ninety-five percent of months fall. With fewer than eight points, the limits are not drawn.

steps.label: Bias, all months
steps.say: To avoid cheating, each year is held out in turn: k is fitted on the other years and applied to the hidden year. Across all 177 held-out months, the bias is minus 0.046. Harmonised MODIS is 4.5 percent lower than VIIRS on average.

steps.label: Spread, all months
steps.say: The standard deviation is 0.40, so the limits of agreement run from minus 0.84 to plus 0.74. A harmonised month lies between 0.43 and 2.10 times the observed value, ninety-five percent of the time.

steps.label: Bias, October and November
steps.say: In the burning season alone, October and November, the bias shrinks to minus 0.010, with a standard deviation of 0.18. Agreement is much tighter where most fires are, and the gate, a bias of at most 0.1 either way, is met.

beats.say: Each point is one held-out overlap month: the log difference between harmonised MODIS and observed VIIRS, plotted against the size of the month. The solid line is the bias, and the dashed lines are the ninety-five percent limits.
The red points, October and November, sit tightly around zero. The quiet months scatter more, because their counts are small.

beats.label: Gates summary
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, open the Validation page. The gates summary lists each test that the harmonised record has to pass, with its threshold.

beats.label: Results
beats.say: The results show the outcomes. Agreement is always measured on held-out years, never on the years used to fit k, because agreement on your own training data would be circular.

points: Limits of agreement [−0.84, +0.74], on held-out years

beats.say: So, to remember: compare harmonised and observed months on a log scale, report the average difference and the band around it, and always test on years the model did not see.
